author: MurmuredVelpro
body:
## What happens

On the Codex (Responses API) → Anthropic Messages path, `internal/gateway/responses.go` demotes `system`/`developer` input items that appear **after the first reply** into a `user` message wrapped in `<system-reminder>`. This was introduced deliberately for cache preservation (#502 — mid-turn context updates shouldn't invalidate the cached prefix).

## Downstream effect

Standing rules that Codex injects as developer items — `AGENTS.md` content, language directives, formatting constraints — are treated by Claude as advisory user text instead of binding system-level instructions. In practice:

- `claude-haiku-5-5` (factory provider) repeatedly violated explicit rules: emitted time estimates the rules forbid, paused mid-task asking for permission to continue, and **answered in Korean** despite an explicit reply-in-the-user's-language rule.
- `claude-sonnet-5-5` showed the same category of violations.
- `gpt-5-6-luna` on the same gateway obeys the same AGENTS.md correctly — its rules never leave the `instructions` field, so they retain system-level weight.

## Why this matters

The failure mode is silent and intermittent: the model *has* the rule text (it can recite it when asked) but doesn't weight it as an instruction, so violations surface randomly — language switching, rule non-compliance, repetition. There's no error anywhere; everything "works".

## Proposal

An opt-in fidelity mode for callers who prefer correctness over cache stability:

- keep caller `developer`/`system` items in the top-level `system` field (accepting the cache rewrite cost #502 avoided), or
- a per-provider/per-route flag to choose fidelity vs. cache-preserving demotion.

Related: #1378 (caller-owned system prompt for subscription adapters), #2322 (Chat Completions keeps mid-conversation system messages in place — same root, different path).
title: Responses→Claude: mid-turn developer/system items demoted to <system-reminder> user turns — agents ignore standing rules, language drift
